blocking_methods.instructions: Call +91 8065 662000 and follow the IVR to hotlist the card.
Email customercare@jana.bank.in from your registered email to request card blocking.
Log in to internet banking at https://ebanking.jana.bank.in/ib-retail-web/tenant/index and use the card block/hotlist option.

Block via the bank's mobile app (Cards > Block/Hotlist). Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.janabank.mtc | iOS: https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/jana-bank-mobile-banking/id1404229430?ls=1&mt=8

Banking Customer Care toll-free 1800 2080 is published as 24x7 and is the number the debit-card page names for blocking ('You can also block your debit card by calling our Customer Care at: 1800 2080 (Toll-free)'). The fraud-reporting page gives both published numbers for reporting a fraudulent transaction: Banking Toll Free 1800 2080 (24/7) or MFI Toll Free 1800 4200 (7 a.m. to 10 p.m.). Customers calling from abroad are directed to +91 8065 662000. No SMS block format is published. In the mobile app or internet banking (ebanking.jana.bank.in): Services -> Debit Card Management -> 'Block Card' (temporary) or 'Hotlist Card' (permanent), select the card number, enter the OTP sent to the registered mobile number and Submit. The published customer-care email is customercare@jana.bank.in. The bank's site now lives at jana.bank.in (www.janabank.com redirects there). The bank's own pages do not mention the national cybercrime helpline 1930.

No credit-card product or credit-card blocking channel is published: the bank's Cards section lists only the RuPay Debit Card, https://www.jana.bank.in/credit-cards/ returned 404 in the same live check, and the only 'credit card' mentions on the FAQ page are generic mobile-banking copy (e.g. changing a 'debit/credit card pin'). The earlier entry's credit-card numbers (1800-102-3456, 080-6956-8800) appear nowhere on the current official site; the banking customer-care lines under 'debit' are the bank's published reporting channels.
